questions.q: What does the Metadata API move, as distinct from REST API, SOQL, or Bulk API?
options: Record data — rows and field values
Only user login credentials
The org's own configuration — object/field definitions, Apex, Flows, Permission Sets, and similar components
Only Lightning Web Component JavaScript files
questions.explain: The Metadata API moves configuration that describes how the org behaves (CustomObject, ApexClass, Flow, PermissionSet, etc.), while REST, SOQL, and Bulk API move record data.

options: A category of record data, like Account or Contact
A user permission level
A kind of scratch org definition file
A specific category of configuration component, such as CustomObject, ApexClass, or Flow, each with its own XML schema
questions.explain: A metadata type is a category of configuration component with its own schema defining what attributes a component of that type can have — CustomObject, ApexClass, and Flow are all examples.

questions.q: What does Salesforce's Metadata Coverage Report tell you?
options: Which metadata types support which API operations (full support, retrieve-only, or partial support)
How many records exist in each custom object
Which Apex classes have test coverage above 75%
Which scratch orgs are nearing their Dev Hub's active org limit
questions.explain: The Metadata Coverage Report lists every metadata type and its level of API support — some types are fully supported for both Metadata API and Tooling API, others are retrieve-only or only partially supported.

options: The npm package manifest for the Salesforce CLI itself
A manifest naming specific metadata components or entire types (via wildcards) to retrieve or deploy via the Metadata API
A file listing a scratch org's installed packages
The project's primary source code file
questions.explain: package.xml is the manifest file that names metadata components or types — using either specific member names or wildcards — that raw Metadata API deploy/retrieve calls operate on.

questions.q: In a package.xml <types> block, what does `<members>*</members>` mean compared to `<members>MyController</members>`?
options: * retrieves zero components, while a named member retrieves all of them
They are functionally identical in every case
* is a wildcard meaning "every component of this type," while a named member targets one specific component by name
* only works for the ApexClass metadata type
questions.explain: A wildcard * requests every component of the given metadata type, while a specific member name like MyController targets just that one named component.
